method: Audited all 42 remaining N5 dictionary entries without prepared exercise links. Created one distinct contextual exercise focused on each entry, with two or three grammar points; these structural entries can also occur together as supporting vocabulary.

After authoring, separately reviewed every sentence, both translations, grammar tags, dictionary links, readings, and production hints. Each entry below records its individual review findings and corrections.

Kept vocabulary IDs and introduction levels unchanged. Forty exercises use N5 content only. Two are explicitly N4: the observed-feeling suffix uses N4 がる grammar, and the nationality exercise uses the existing N4 supporting word アメリカ. Coverage counts include both levels, as in the original audit.

Added usable affix/counter forms with grammatical part-of-speech matching, protected ordinary noun senses from counter homophones, and preserved grammatical particle categories. Extended opt-in whole-word tokenization to interjections and retained the existing numeric-boundary guard for dates and counts.

Restricted reading-only fallback for counters and affixes so honorific ご cannot match language ～語. Added regression checks for this homophone, adjective くらい versus approximation, book versus 本 counter, general time versus measured hours, person-count/nationality readings, greetings, and irregular dates. Corrected the older 一日中 vocabulary example with explicit じゅう reading and the time-wide suffix link.

Corrected the English/French meanings of the nationality suffix じん, time-wide じゅう, and existential 在る. Kept コピー as a noun distinct from the existing コピーする verb; the new copies exercise explicitly selects the noun.

Existing Japanese sentences, translations, grammar tags, level assignments, audio paths, and speech text remain unchanged. Sixteen target entries gain links in existing exercises. Source overrides preserve the existing とき noun in eleven ambiguous 時 contexts.

Validated every final recording as audible PCM, independently transcribed all 42 without expected-text prompts, and made a second independent transcription with only a hiragana-formatting instruction. Corrected and regenerated ambiguous readings, a tense revision, and a recording with excessive silence. All final phonetic transcripts agree with the complete prepared reading after punctuation, katakana, and residual-kanji normalization.

Rendered all 42 exercises in English and French in Chromium at a 390-pixel mobile viewport. Opened every production hint, checked dictionary IDs and hint-credit exclusions, grammar explanations, prompts, answers, overflow, audio buttons, decoding, and representative playback. Visually inspected the final French copies exercise.
